reflections.title: "My Soul Thirsts for You"

reflect.text: Real physical thirst is impossible to ignore. It cuts through every distraction until we find something to drink. Yet in our spiritual lives, daily busyness and everyday duties can easily keep us from noticing how dry our souls have become. When times are comfortable, our desire for God often fades. We can easily be tempted to chase lesser things or rely on outward religious routines that never truly satisfy our hearts.

God sometimes allows us to walk through dry, lonely wilderness seasons for our good. Experiencing our lack shows us our true condition and pushes us to seek Him with urgency. When David was in danger and alone in the desert, he did not turn to false comforts first. He sought God. Spending steady time in prayer and reading Scripture sharpens our appetite for Him. Tasting His steadfast love proves that knowing Him is better than anything this earthly life can offer.

questions: What earthly comforts are you tempted to turn to when your heart feels dry?
How can setting aside time for prayer and Scripture today help you seek God first?
reflections.prayer: Lord, forgive us when busyness and comfort dull our appetite for You. In our dry and lonely moments, teach us not to turn to empty substitutes. Satisfy our thirsty souls with Your faithful love, which is better than life. Amen.

reflections.title: Following Hard After God

reflect.text: When David writes that his soul clings to God, the words picture someone staying close in eager pursuit. In a dry wilderness where water is scarce, imagine a guide who knows a hidden, cool spring. The guide invites the thirsty traveler to follow, and the traveler stays right on his heels. In the same way, God Himself stirs our thirst and comes to guide us to His refreshing love through Jesus Christ.

Like Jonathan's armor-bearer who climbed up steep rocks right behind his leader, we are called to stay close to our Savior. Following Christ is not always easy. The path may lead over steep hills, through rough brush, and into harsh winds. Yet as F. B. Meyer reminds us, we should "let there be no needless space between the Master and thee." As we press on after Jesus, God's strong hand holds us up, bringing real joy even in the wilderness.

questions: Is there any distance right now between you and Jesus as you walk through your daily routine?
What difficult path are you facing today where you need to follow close behind the Lord?
reflections.prayer: Lord, thank You for coming to lead us to the living water our souls need. Give us courage to follow close behind Jesus, even when the path is rough. Hold us up by Your strong hand and fill our hearts with joy. Amen.
